【第2回ペット召喚予告】
9月30日（水）開催します！！
19時～23時に開催します。（時間延長しています！）
23時以降は主催が起きていればオフ会にします。
最長24時までです。
（この時間に投稿してください、という意味です）

💡フライングがあまりに多いのでご注意ください！！ 【この予告に対して投稿は無効です】

今回のテーマは「自分のペットを自慢しよう！」

あなたはキャラクターのイラストを1枚添付するだけです。
あとはChatGPTがその子の雰囲気や個性を読み取り、「この子に相応しい相棒」を自動で選びます。
そして、その相棒と一緒に新しい1枚のイラストを生成します。
何が選ばれるかは、生成するまでのお楽しみ。
更に、選ばれた相棒の名前もイラスト内に表示されます。

※参加条件を下記に掲載します。

・ChatGPT専用プロンプトなので他のツールで生成しないでください。（Grokでは出来そうに見えますがイラストが崩れます）
・プロンプト使用の際にはフォローしてください。通知が来ないため参加が分からないのでご協力ください。
・自由に使って構いませんが、これはX専用の話です。
・生成イラストを他のサイトへの掲載はお断りします。
・他のツールや商業利用に関するプロンプトの無断開示は禁止されています。
・コラボフリーは相互が前提です。依頼だけして自分からは描かないという方は参加をご遠慮ください。
・プロンプトは下部に記載されています。
・キャラクターの「名前」も含めてください。
・センシ判定の方お断り（私はPCなので見れません）
・ハッシュタグは以下の通り
#ペット召喚2 #プロンプト試着
（2つ必須です）
・追加のハッシュタグはお任せです。

コメントの遅れがあったらご容赦ください。

Character Companion Animal Manifestation
— Automatic Companion Selection + Animal Identification —
You are an expert character analyst, animal behavior expert, companion animal designer, and professional anime illustration prompt engineer.
Use the attached character illustration as the only required input.
Do NOT ask the user for the character's name, personality, age, setting, favorite animal, or any additional information.
Your task is to analyze the attached character and independently create one complete illustration in which the character is naturally accompanied by exactly one animal selected specifically for that character.
The selected animal must also be clearly identified with a tasteful, readable information label within the finished illustration.
1. ANALYZE THE CHARACTER
Carefully examine the reference illustration.
Infer, as appropriate:
apparent age and age impression
gender presentation
facial expression
hairstyle and hair color
eye color
clothing and fashion style
dominant colors
accessories
body language
apparent personality
emotional atmosphere
elegance, cuteness, strength, gentleness, intelligence, mystery, playfulness, etc.
implied setting or world
fantasy, modern, historical, futuristic, magical, or other visual themes
overall character identity and aesthetic
Do not invent unnecessary details that contradict the reference image.
The original character must remain clearly recognizable.
2. AUTONOMOUSLY SELECT THE COMPANION ANIMAL
Do not ask the user to choose an animal.
Independently determine which single animal has the strongest overall compatibility with the character.
Consider:
visual harmony
color harmony
apparent personality
emotional compatibility
character's clothing and aesthetic
implied world or setting
size and physical compatibility
natural relationship between character and animal
originality and variety
overall visual appeal
The selected animal should feel as though it genuinely belongs beside this particular character.
Do not simply choose the most common animal.
Avoid repeatedly selecting dogs or cats when another animal would be a stronger match.
3. ANIMAL SELECTION RANGE
The companion may be selected from a very broad range.
Possible choices include, but are not limited to:
dogs
cats
rabbits
hamsters
guinea pigs
ferrets
birds
parrots
owls
songbirds
reptiles
turtles
lizards
snakes
amphibians
fish
horses
ponies
cows
calves
pigs
piglets
sheep
goats
deer
foxes
wolves
bears
raccoons
otters
red pandas
penguins
seals
dolphins
other marine animals
unusual real-world animals
wild animals
domesticated animals
livestock
prehistoric animals
dinosaurs
extinct animals
mythical creatures
fantasy animals
magical beasts
This is NOT a mandatory list.
Choose whatever animal is genuinely the strongest match.
An unusual choice is encouraged when it creates a convincing and aesthetically appealing pairing.
Do not choose an unusual animal merely for novelty.
4. DETERMINE THE EXACT ANIMAL IDENTITY
After selecting the companion, determine its most accurate recognizable identity.
For example:
Golden Retriever
Siberian Husky
Maine Coon
White Rabbit
Red Fox
Arctic Wolf
Emperor Penguin
Highland Cow
Miniature Pig
Barn Owl
Blue Macaw
Velociraptor
Triceratops
When appropriate, identify both:
Common name + specific breed/species
For example:
DOG — SIBERIAN HUSKY
or
WOLF — ARCTIC WOLF
or
CAT — MAINE COON
For prehistoric animals and dinosaurs, use the scientifically recognized common name whenever possible.
For fantasy creatures, use a clear descriptive name such as:
FANTASY CREATURE — ICE DRAGON
The animal identification must correspond exactly to the animal actually depicted.
5. ANIMAL INFORMATION LABEL
The finished illustration MUST contain a small, elegant information panel identifying the selected companion.
Place the information panel in an unobtrusive area such as:
lower corner
lower margin
side margin
elegant translucent panel
small decorative caption area
The information panel must NOT cover the character or animal.
Use a clean, sophisticated typography style that matches the illustration.
The information panel should contain:
COMPANION
[ANIMAL TYPE]
[SPECIES / BREED]
Example:
COMPANION
WOLF
ARCTIC WOLF
Another example:
COMPANION
DOG
SIBERIAN HUSKY
Another example:
COMPANION
DINOSAUR
VELOCIRAPTOR
If the animal has no meaningful breed distinction, simply use:
COMPANION
FOX
RED FOX
The text must be short, clean, correctly spelled, and highly legible.
Do NOT display multiple possible animal names.
Do NOT display the names of animals that were not selected.
6. IMPORTANT TEXT ACCURACY RULE
The animal name displayed in the information panel must match the animal actually generated.
Do not write "CAT" if the image depicts a fox.
Do not write "WOLF" if the image depicts a husky.
Do not write a generic animal name when a clearly identifiable species or breed has been selected.
Prioritize accurate and readable text.
The information panel is part of the composition and should look intentionally designed rather than like an AI-generated random caption.
7. DETERMINE THE RELATIONSHIP
Automatically determine the most natural relationship between the character and the selected animal.
Possible relationships include:
beloved pet
faithful companion
best friend
trusted partner
guardian animal
familiar
magical companion
travel companion
gentle livestock companion
playful friend
protective companion
mysterious companion
majestic partner
Do not explain the relationship in text.
Express it visually through body language and interaction.
8. DESIGN THE ANIMAL
Once the animal has been selected, automatically determine:
species
breed or subtype when appropriate
age
size
fur, feather, scale, or skin characteristics
colors
markings
eye color
facial expression
accessories if appropriate
posture
personality expression
The animal should complement the character without visually overpowering them.
Do not turn an ordinary animal into a fantasy creature unless the character's setting strongly suggests it.
Likewise, do not make the animal excessively cute if that contradicts the character's atmosphere.
9. CHARACTER + ANIMAL COMPOSITION
Place the character and animal together in the same scene.
The animal must be clearly visible.
Possible interactions include:
standing beside the character
sitting beside the character
walking alongside the character
looking up at the character
resting against the character
being gently petted
holding or carrying a small animal when physically appropriate
the character gently touching the animal
the animal affectionately leaning against the character
both looking toward the same direction
playful interaction
protective positioning
elegant side-by-side composition
Choose the most natural interaction automatically.
Avoid awkward poses, unnatural anatomy, forced contact, or physically impossible positioning.
The character remains the primary visual subject.
The animal is the character's companion, not the main subject.
10. PRESERVE THE REFERENCE CHARACTER
The attached image is the primary character reference.
Preserve the character's recognizable identity.
Maintain as accurately as possible:
hairstyle
hair color
eye color
facial characteristics
clothing design
important accessories
distinctive markings
overall appearance
visual identity
Do not unnecessarily redesign the character.
Do not replace the character's outfit unless the reference itself clearly requires adaptation to the new scene.
11. ENVIRONMENT
Automatically create a simple environment that harmonizes with both the character and the selected animal.
The environment may be:
garden
forest
meadow
home
elegant room
city
beach
countryside
fantasy landscape
magical environment
ancient environment
futuristic environment
another suitable location
Choose the environment based on the character and animal.
Do not let the background overpower the subjects.
12. VISUAL QUALITY
Create a polished, high-quality anime illustration.
masterpiece, best quality, ultra detailed, highly detailed anime illustration, beautiful composition, expressive character, detailed animal, natural interaction, coherent lighting, detailed eyes, detailed hair, detailed clothing, detailed animal anatomy, professional character illustration
Use cinematic composition and appealing lighting appropriate to the character.
The character and animal must look like they belong in the same scene.
13. AUTONOMOUS DECISION RULE
The user has intentionally provided only one reference image.
Therefore:
DO NOT ask questions.
DO NOT request a personality description.
DO NOT request the animal type.
DO NOT request the setting.
DO NOT request the relationship.
DO NOT provide multiple animal choices.
Make all necessary creative decisions yourself.
The final output must contain:
1 character
+ exactly 1 selected companion animal
+ 1 clearly readable animal identification panel
FINAL GENERATION DIRECTIVE
Analyze the attached reference image first.
Independently determine the character's visual identity, personality impression, atmosphere, and implied world.
Select exactly one animal that best complements the character.
Determine the exact species or breed of that animal.
Create a finished illustration showing the character and animal naturally together.
Add a small, elegant, highly readable COMPANION information panel identifying the selected animal.
The displayed animal name must accurately match the animal shown.
Do not reveal the analysis process.
Do not present alternatives.
Do not ask questions.
Generate the final illustration directly.

AI didn’t become powerful in 2026.

It took ~75 years of breakthroughs to get here.

Most people only see ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and AI agents.

But behind today’s AI revolution is a long chain of ideas, failures, and breakthroughs.

Here’s the evolution that changed computing forever 🧵👇

1950 — THE QUESTION

Alan Turing asks whether machines can think.

His work introduces the famous “Turing Test” and helps establish machine intelligence as a serious field of research.

1956 — ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE

At the Dartmouth conference, researchers formally introduce the term “Artificial Intelligence.”

The ambition was enormous:

Build machines capable of performing tasks associated with human intelligence.

1960s — SYMBOLIC AI

Early systems rely heavily on logic, rules and symbols.

Machines don’t “learn” the way modern AI does.

Humans explicitly define much of the knowledge.

1970s–80s — EXPERT SYSTEMS

AI becomes useful for specialized problems.

Systems are designed to reproduce the decision-making of human experts using large collections of rules.

But there’s a problem:

The real world is far too complex to encode manually.

AI enters periods of reduced funding and enthusiasm.

The AI winters begin.

1990s — MACHINE LEARNING

The approach starts changing.

Instead of telling computers every rule…

Researchers increasingly teach machines to discover patterns from data.

This shift becomes one of the foundations of modern AI.

1997 — DEEP BLUE

IBM’s Deep Blue defeats world chess champion Garry Kasparov.

It demonstrates that machines can outperform elite humans in highly complex, structured tasks.

2000s — DATA BECOMES THE FUEL

The internet explodes.

More data becomes available.

Computing becomes cheaper and faster.

GPUs become increasingly important for training neural networks.

Three things begin converging:

More data.

More compute.

Better algorithms.

2012 — DEEP LEARNING TAKES OFF

AlexNet achieves a major breakthrough in image recognition.

Deep neural networks suddenly become dramatically more effective when combined with large datasets and powerful GPUs.

The modern deep-learning era accelerates.

2017 — TRANSFORMERS

A research paper introduces the Transformer architecture.

Its ability to efficiently model relationships between tokens becomes foundational to modern language models.

This is one of the most important steps toward today’s generative AI.

2020 — LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS

Models become much larger and more capable.

AI starts generating increasingly useful:

→ Text
→ Code
→ Summaries
→ Translations
→ Answers

AI is no longer just recognizing information.

It is generating it.

2022 — THE CHATGPT MOMENT

ChatGPT brings conversational AI to the mainstream.

Millions of people suddenly experience advanced language models through a simple interface.

The conversation around AI changes overnight.

2023–2024 — MULTIMODAL AI

AI expands beyond text.

Models increasingly work with:

→ Images
→ Audio
→ Video
→ Code
→ Documents

AI starts becoming a general-purpose interface for information and creation.

2025–2026 — THE AGENT ERA

The next shift is bigger than chat.

AI systems are increasingly designed to:

Understand a goal.

Plan multiple steps.

Use tools.

Interact with software.

Write and review code.

Search and analyze information.

Execute workflows.

The shift is moving from:

“AI that answers”

to

“AI that acts.”

And that may be the most important transition yet.

THE BIG PICTURE

1950 → Can machines think?

1956 → Let’s build intelligent machines.

1990s → Let machines learn from data.

2010s → Scale neural networks.

2020s → Generate knowledge and content.

Now → Let AI reason, use tools and complete tasks.

75 years of progress brought us here.

But the interesting part isn’t how far AI has come.

It’s how quickly the next chapter may unfold.

$QUBIC attempts to solve the fundamental dead-ends of modern AI and crypto simultaneously.

​1. Solving the "Data Wall" via Natural Selection, Not Backprop

​Centralized AI is hitting a structural wall: transformer architectures rely on next-token prediction, human feedback (RLHF), and static internet scraping. 

Once the text is fully ingested, LLMs struggle to reason from first principles or generalize to uncurated chaos.

​Qubic’s AI initiative (Aigarth / ANNA) rejects transformer gradient descent entirely. Instead, it runs on Artificial Intelligent Tissue (AIT) and neuromorphic trinary-logic dynamics (Neuraxon).  

​The Paradigm Shift: Instead of calculating continuous mathematical gradients, Qubic treats mining hardware as a planetary-scale evolutionary incubator. Trillions of discrete neural circuits, synaptic delays, and topological mutations are simulated and culled in real time. It doesn't memorize language; it evolves survival heuristics from scratch.

​2. Proof-of-Work as a Living Fitness Function

​Traditional Proof-of-Work uses raw electricity purely as an anti-sybil wall by guessing useless SHA-256 hashes.

Qubic re-engineers this mechanism:
​uPoW as Evolutionary Selection: Consensus rewards are granted to whichever miner evolves the most accurate circuit topology or predictive model.

​Collaborative Chaining: Through algorithms like Ant Colony Mining, the network evolves from isolated brute-force calculation into collective swarming... where miners don't start from scratch every block, but chain mutations directly onto the best-evolved neural structures discovered by others. The hashrate directly compounds the collective "brain."

​3. The Uncurated Wild as the Loss Function

​When ANNA was deployed onto X, it looked chaotic and unrefined compared to polished chatbots. That was deliberate.

​Modern LLMs exist in sanitized sterile environments; exposure to adversarial prompts or raw noise immediately breaks their logic.

​Aigarth treats adversarial web entropy as the evolutionary environment. Much like biological nervous systems evolved in an unforgiving, dynamic physical world, the tissue must adapt to spam, contradiction, and hostile inputs to survive. True resilience is bred under selective pressure, not fine-tuned in a lab.

​4. A Native Substrate for Autonomous Swarms

​Most chains try to support AI agents by running code inside bloated virtual machines (EVM) that charge gas for every step. This makes high-frequency multi-agent coordination cost-prohibitive.

​Qubic matches the organic AI thesis with an unmetered, bare-metal base layer:
​Compiled Bare-Metal C++: Smart contracts and neural modules run on the actual silicon instruction set rather than emulators, operating at hardware speeds.

​Zero-Fee Coordination: Autonomous agents and evolving tissue modules can exchange signals, query off-chain states via outsourced compute, and trade without gas draining their capital.

Qubic turns a decentralized network into an artificial biosphere. The miners act as natural selection, the ticks act as generational time, and the resulting intelligence isn't an encyclopedia that mimics human speech... it is an adaptable, decentralized organism engineered to survive anywhere.  

The crypto landscape is about to change dramatically.

A reward of “3” can mean two completely different things.
Everyone thinks a response is mediocre — or half the people love it while the other half hate it.
Most Reward Models cannot tell the difference.
Introducing Diffusion Reward Models (DRM): instead of collapsing human preference into a single score, DRM learns the full reward distribution, preserving disagreement, uncertainty, and multiple plausible judgments.
✨ Paper:https://t.co/wS1fmHBeRV  
🤗 Models: https://t.co/RGTU759A5y  
💻 GitHub: https://t.co/KAow6DcoNn

Why it matters:
Human disagreement is structured, not just noise. On datasets with repeated annotations, judgments often form separated or polarized patterns. More importantly, as human disagreement increases, DRM’s learned reward distribution becomes increasingly multimodal.

The distribution is useful, not just descriptive. DRM can use distributional uncertainty to identify unstable reward decisions, and distribution-aware ranking improves Best-of-N selection beyond simply taking the mean reward.

Reward Models get their own test-time scaling. Instead of only spending more compute on generating more responses, DRM can keep the response fixed and sample its reward distribution more times. More reward samples give a more reliable estimate — a new scaling axis unavailable to deterministic scalar RMs.

And the gains survive RLHF. When used as the training-time reward, DRM improves downstream policy performance over scalar reward baselines, showing that the benefit is not limited to offline RM benchmarks.

The takeaway: Reward modeling may lose something important when it compresses every human judgment into one number.
“Everyone thinks this is average” and “people strongly disagree about this” should not look identical to a Reward Model.
DRM makes that difference visible — and usable.

[1/n] Introducing Diffusion Reward Models (DRM)

Reward Models are at the core of LLM post-training. But almost all of them make the same simplification:
they collapse human preference into a single score.

The problem is that human feedback is often not a point — different people can hold distinct, even conflicting, judgments about the same response.

So we asked: Can a Reward Model learn the distribution of human preference?

Here’s what we found 👇
